name: WP Affiliate Disclosure
author: mojofywp

sections.description:
Live Demo: https://www.mojofywp.com/wp-affiliate-disclosure/demo

If you’re an affiliate marketer, blogger, or website owner, and you’re promoting products of companies from US, UK, or Canada, the FTC (Federal Trade Commission) requires you to tell your visitors that you will be compensated if they purchase something through your affiliate link(s).

However, adding the disclosure statement manually into each posts would be a hassle – But worries no more…

WP Affiliate Disclosure allows you to add a customizable, FTC-compliant disclosure statement that will automatically display across your WordPress website based on the rule(s) you define.

Main features:

  • Show the disclosure statement at the beginning and/or the end of a post.
  • Easily customize statement content, including adding in links, images, as well as HTML elements.
  • Only show the disclosure statement on certain posts.
  • Only show the disclosure statement based on its taxonomies ( categories / tags )
  • Works on custom post type as well

Live Demo: https://www.mojofywp.com/wp-affiliate-disclosure/demo
sections.installation:
1. Unzip the downloaded zip file.
  2. Upload the plugin folder into the wp-content/plugins/ directory of your WordPress site.
  3. Activate WP Affiliate Disclosure from Plugins page
sections.faq:
My disclosure is not showing on any posts

Check that you have a published rule, the display position is enabled, the post type and conditions match the post you are viewing, and any page or CDN caches have been cleared. Some custom themes and builder templates bypass WordPress’s standard content filter; in those cases, use shortcode placement or test with a default WordPress theme.

My disclosure shows on the wrong pages

Review the rule conditions. Use taxonomy slugs for category or tag targeting, post IDs for individual posts, and priority ordering when multiple rules can match the same post.

Can I change the disclosure statement?

Yes. You can.

Can I add links into the statement?

Yes. You can.

Can I add images into the statement?

Yes. You can.

Can I limit to which post the statement is shown?

Yes. You can.

Can I specify which post the disclosure statement should display?

Yes. You can.

Can I specify only posts with a certain categories that should show the disclosure statement?

Yes. You can.

Is the plugin compatible with all WordPress themes?

WP Affiliate Disclosure is compatible with most of the themes that follow wordpress coding practices and standards. However, since every wordpress themes has its own coding structure, it’s pretty difficult to promise that this plugin will absolutely work with just any themes in the market.

Does the plugin work with Oxygen Builder?

Oxygen Builder renders post content through its own template pipeline and does not call WordPress’s standard the_content filter. This means automatic filter-based disclosure insertion will not work for pages built with Oxygen. To add a disclosure on Oxygen-built pages, use the Affiliate Disclosure block directly inside your Oxygen template, or insert the [affiliate_disclosure] shortcode in a Code Block element within your Oxygen layout.

Does version 1.5 change anything for the Classic Editor?

No. Automatic disclosures, the [wpadc] and [affiliate_disclosure] shortcodes and your rules work exactly as before. The block, sidebar and patterns only appear in the Block Editor.

What happens if I add the block to a post that already has an automatic rule?

The block wins. The post shows one disclosure: the block’s. Automatic insertion is skipped for that post only when the block would actually show a disclosure; an empty or broken block never removes your automatic disclosure.

Where is Import / Export?

Under WP Affiliate Disclosure > Tools in the WordPress admin menu. Export downloads a JSON file with your rules, templates, settings and styling. Import shows a preview of what will change before anything is written. Choose Merge to add to the existing rules or Replace to overwrite them; Replace saves a backup of what it overwrote, which you can download.

Moving settings between sites

Export on the old site, then import the file on the new site. Rules that target specific posts or terms are matched by slug on the new site; anything that cannot be found is listed in the preview as a warning so you can fix it. Files made by a newer version of the plugin are refused with a clear message.

Per-post overrides apply to the post, not to one rule

In the editor sidebar you can disable the disclosure for a post or override its text, placement or style. An override applies to every automatic rule that matches that post. If you set a placement, only the first matching rule (by priority) is shown, once, at that position. If you set only the text and two rules match (one before, one after), both show the override text. The [wpadc] shortcode in the post also uses the override text and style unless the shortcode sets its own text, template, style or rule attribute; [wpadc rule="N"] always shows rule N’s own text and style.

I put the disclosure block in a header or footer template part

Block themes can place the block in a template part. Header: the block’s disclosure is shown and the automatic one is skipped. Footer: both may show (a duplicate, never a missing disclosure). To stop the duplicate, add add_filter( 'wpadc_post_has_disclosure_block', '__return_true' ); for the affected post types, turn on “Disable for this post”, or use a rule whose position is shortcode only.

I hid the disclosure block (or the group it is in)

A block hidden with the editor’s Hide option, or hidden on some screen sizes, does not count as a disclosure. The automatic disclosure is shown instead, so it is never missing. If the block is hidden only on some screen sizes, both disclosures may show on the screen sizes where the block is visible. To avoid that, leave the block visible everywhere or turn on “Disable for this post”.

What happens to the block if I deactivate the plugin or go back to 1.4?

The block also saves a plain-text copy of its disclosure in the post. While the plugin (1.5 or later) is active, the copy is never shown: the block is rendered fresh with your current text and style. If the plugin is deactivated, or rolled back to 1.4.x (which does not know the block), WordPress shows the plain-text copy instead, so the post still has a disclosure. The copy is updated each time you save the post in the block editor; if you later change a rule’s or template’s text, the copy keeps the old text until the post is saved again. If such a post also matches an automatic rule in 1.4.x, both may show.

Developers: emptying the block with the wpadc_block_render filter

If a wpadc_block_render filter returns an empty string for a disclosure block in the post content, the plugin still treats the post as having a block and skips the automatic disclosure, so the post shows none. When your filter empties a block, also return false from wpadc_post_has_disclosure_block for that post so the automatic disclosure is shown.

Is the plugin translation ready?

Yes, absolutely! The plugin comes with a PO file that you can use to translate WP Affiliate Disclosure to any desired language.
sections.changelog:
1.5.0

  • New: Affiliate Disclosure block with Boxed, Banner and Inline style variations.
  • New: Editor sidebar panel showing the matching rule, with per-post overrides (disable, text, placement, style).
  • New: Four block patterns (Standard FTC, Amazon Affiliate Notice, Sponsored Post Header, Minimal Inline).
  • New: Import / Export (Tools) for rules, templates, settings and styling as JSON, with a preview before anything changes.
  • Improved: A valid disclosure block on a post prevents a second automatic disclosure.
  • Improved: Automatic disclosures never disappear because of an empty or broken block (fail-safe).
  • Improved: The disclosure block saves a plain-text copy of its text, shown only if the plugin is deactivated or rolled back to 1.4.x, so the post keeps a disclosure.
  • Fixed: Free version limits now also apply to the REST API, Tools import and per-post placement overrides: after-paragraph, shortcode and widget placements, extra post types, exclusion filters and more than one rule need the premium version. Imports into a free site keep one rule and list what was skipped or removed.
  • Fixed: The Help page marks premium-only placement guides as Premium on the free version.
  • Fixed: The editor sidebar no longer says an empty or hidden disclosure block handles the disclosure.
  • Fixed: [wpadc rule="N"] shows rule N’s own text and style, also on a post with per-post overrides.
  • Fixed: A rule can no longer be saved without a post type. A rule created through the REST API keeps the default settings for anything the request leaves out.
  • Changed: Per-post placement overrides use the hyphen form (before-content, after-content), the same as rules. The underscore forms (before_content, after_content) are still accepted when saving and are converted. Any other value is rejected with a 400 rest_not_in_enum error.
  • Security: The getting-started wizard and the rule list refresh on the Overview page now require an administrator.
  • Security: Disclosure rules can only be read, created, edited or deleted by administrators, on every WordPress path including XML-RPC.
  • Security: Rule text saved from the rule editor and the wizard is filtered the same way as in the REST API and import, and rule priority is stored as a number.
  • Security: These issues also affect 1.4.x. Updating is recommended.
  • Updated: Requires WordPress 6.6 or higher for the block editor features. On older WordPress your existing rules, shortcodes and automatic disclosures keep working, and you will see an update notice.
  • Classic Editor: works exactly as before.
  • Compatibility: Tested up to WordPress 7.1.5.

1.4.1

  • Updated: Freemius SDK to 2.13.5.
  • Compatibility: Tested up to WordPress 7.1.3.

1.4.0

  • New: Visual styling controls in the rule editor — pick from 4 presets (Minimal, Boxed, Banner, Inline) or customize colors, borders, padding, and margin without writing CSS.
  • New: After-paragraph placement — show the disclosure after paragraph 1, 2, or 3.
  • New: One-click disclosure templates for Amazon Associates and General FTC compliance (short and long variants).
  • New: [affiliate_disclosure] shortcode alias with style, template, variant, text, and rule attributes.
  • New: REST API CRUD endpoints — POST/PUT/DELETE /wpadc/v1/rules and PUT /wpadc/v1/rules/reorder for programmatic rule management.
  • New: Admin notices when a rule has no targeting conditions or no rules exist (per-user dismissible).
  • Fixed: Disclosure no longer injected in widgets, REST output, excerpts, or featured-image processing — main-loop guard added to all the_content callbacks.
  • Fixed: Autoloader failure now shows a helpful admin notice instead of a white screen.
  • Compatibility: id="wpadc-wrapper" is now emitted on the first disclosure wrapper per page only — preserving backward-compatible CSS for sites with a single disclosure per page. Pages with multiple disclosures (e.g. both before- and after-content placements active) will only see the id on the first wrapper; use .wpadc-wrapper-class or .wpadc-disclosure to target all wrappers. Advanced users can remove the id entirely by returning false from the wpadc_emit_legacy_wrapper_id filter.

upgrade_notice.1.5.0: 1.5.0 adds the Affiliate Disclosure block, an editor sidebar and import/export. The block editor features need WordPress 6.6; on older versions your existing disclosures keep working and you will see an update notice. 1.5.0 also includes security fixes, so updating is recommended. No settings change is needed. Back up with WP Affiliate Disclosure > Tools > Export before upgrading if you manage many rules.
upgrade_notice.1.4.0: v1.4 ships visual styling, after-paragraph placement, disclosure templates, and full REST API CRUD. Compatibility: id="wpadc-wrapper" is preserved on the first disclosure wrapper per page. Sites with multiple disclosures on a single page should migrate custom CSS to .wpadc-wrapper-class or .wpadc-disclosure.
upgrade_notice.1.3.0:
• Improved: Refreshed in-plugin Help and FAQ content.
  • Under the hood: Modernized the build system for future development.
  • Under the hood: Added namespaced service scaffolding and REST API foundations.
  • Updated: Now requires WordPress 5.8+ and PHP 7.4+.
